subject: On-prem module certification & CI handbook

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Clara Gomez <clara.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem module certification & CI handbook

Hi all,

Following up from the pre-flight call with ACME: attached is our initial "On‑Prem IaC Certification" checklist (onprem-iac-cert-checklist.pdf). Goal: produce a lightweight handbook that certifies each Terraform/Helm/Ansible module for on‑prem (VPC + bare‑metal) deployments and a CI pattern that ACME can run in their pipeline.

High‑level asks:
- Internal reviewers: read checklist, mark any gaps for module testing, artifact signing, or network evidence.
- ACME: confirm the evidence types you accept (e.g. terraform plan output, helm-values, signed artifacts).
- Owners: add the specific CI job names + artifact locations we should reference in evidence (e.g. gitlab-job:tf-plan-acme).

Key checklist sections that need early attention: module interface contracts (inputs/outputs), network zoning & egress proof, KMS/HSM key use for secrets, OPA/policy checks, and reproducible dry‑run artifacts.

I've stubbed three attachments we can iterate on: tf-plan-acme-vpc.txt (example plan), helm-values-acme.yaml (recommended defaults), and the PDF checklist.

Can we get first‑pass comments by EOD Tuesday (2027‑06‑01)? I can carve out time to consolidate and produce the handbook draft for ACME.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Product Operations — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Clara Gomez <clara.gomez@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem module certification & CI handbook

Thanks Diego — good start. Quick notes from a module-owner POV: 

- Terraform modules:
  * Please add a "test vector" section per module listing the minimal tfvars to exercise cross‑AZ networking and the expected plan diffs. That makes it trivial for ACME to run a reproducible dry run.
  * Add guidance about state backend (we should insist on remote state with locking for their CI jobs).

- Helm charts:
  * For chart values, include a toggle to disable hostPath mounts and prefer ephemeral volumes by default. I called out two required value keys in the attached helm-values-acme.yaml.
  * Add a simple helm‑template CI job that renders charts with the ACME values file and runs kubeval.

- Ansible roles:
  * Need a verification playbook that runs in a short window (10–15s checks) to validate firewall rules and IP whitelists post‑provision.

On CI specifics: add exact job names we will ask ACME to provide evidence for (e.g., ci/tf/plan-acme, ci/helm/render-acme, ci/ansible/verify-acme). That way we can match artifacts in their audit.

One concrete gap: egress control evidence. The checklist mentions egress rules but not the telemetry artifact (pcap vs. flow logs). We should recommend flow logs + a sample query.

I'll sketch a short template for the module test vector by tomorrow.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Infra PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On-prem module certification & CI handbook

Diego / team—thanks for sending this over. A few clarifications from ACME's side: 

- Evidence types: we accept terraform plan outputs, signed tarballs of rendered helm templates, CI job logs, and flow logs (Cloud/Network provider export). Full pcaps are not necessary.
- For KMS: we use an HSM-backed key service; anything signed with our key needs to include key-id and signature metadata.
- Egress controls: we'll need at least 7 days of flow logs showing the expected closed ports in our staging environment. Can Redwood run a short synthetic traffic test we can trigger from CI?

Also, we prefer separate artifacts per environment (staging vs prod) with a naming convention. I'll attach our evidence template after I confirm with Security.

Happy to meet if you want to walk through one module end‑to‑end.

—Clara
Clara Gomez
Platform Security, ACME Corp.

Subject: Re: On-prem module certification & CI handbook

Thanks — I've attached a small tf plan snapshot (tf-plan-acme-vpc.txt) and added inline comments to the checklist where I think we need stronger gating. Highlights: 

- Premerge CI: require a "ci/tf/plan-acme" job that runs with their tfvars and uploads the plan artifact to an immutable storage location. We should verify the plan artifact signature using their HSM key metadata.
- OPA gates: add a policy for network exposures (no 0.0.0.0/0 on management ports) and require an OPA report artifact in the pipeline.
- Dry-run reproducibility: ensure the plan is produced by a pinned terraform version; include terraform version file in evidence.
- Helm: the helm render job should also run a smoke manifest validation (kubeval + schema) and produce a tar.gz of rendered manifests signed and named like render-acme-<env>-<sha>.tar.gz.

I added a small snippet to the checklist about how to collect flow logs using the common provider exporters and a simple query that ACME can run to show the past 7 days.

Next step: can Karthik and Marissa take ownership of the module test vector template? I'll wire the CI job names into the checklist once we agree.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

I'll own the module test vector template. Couple of practical points: 

- Template fields: module name, minimal tfvars, expected resource counts, negative tests (intentional misconfig), network reachability test steps, and required evidence file names.
- For the Ansible verification playbook we should provide two entrypoints: quick-check (10s) and full-audit (~5m) with clear flags.
- CI integration: recommend GitLab artifacts + a short signed manifest (SHA + key-id) included as metadata.

I'll drop a draft in the INFRA ticket (INFRA-789) by EOD Thursday. If ACME wants a walkthrough, I'm available next Tuesday afternoon.
